read_across: Regulators dominated the week. NHTSA activity around Tesla's Cybercab self-certification, Zoox's robotaxi exemption, Waymo's flooded-road OTA recall and the Recalls Next notice signals a US framework being rewritten around driverless vehicles. In Europe, Volkswagen and Elli's Q4 V2G launch and the IEA's first standalone V2G report coincide with a maturing EU Data Act regime that has moved fleet telematics access closer to a commodity.

Connectivity and cyber signals reinforced each other. Kigen's SGP.32 v1.3 eSIM certification, the Iridium–Deutsche Telekom–Toyota NB-IoT satellite voice demonstration and Thales's five-operator SGP.32 rollout show the eSIM-plus-NTN stack reaching commercial readiness. UN R155/R156, the EU Cyber Resilience Act and Japan's Active Cyber Defence law extend certified CSMS and SBOM obligations from cars to robots, chargers and off-highway machines, with quality and cyber recalls increasingly indistinguishable.

items.headline: NHTSA orders Tesla to justify Cybercab self-certification by 30 September
items.summary: NHTSA issued a Special Order on 10 September under Audit Query AQ26002, demanding sworn answers to 21 questions on how Tesla self-certified the no-wheel, no-pedal Cybercab as FMVSS-compliant. Around 1,000 units operate in Austin; responses were due 30 September 2026.
items.so_what: First formal US challenge to self-certification of a purpose-built driverless vehicle already carrying paying riders.

items.headline: Volkswagen recalls 49,958 MY2025 Tiguans over BCM software that can stall engine
items.summary: NHTSA campaign 26V587 covers 49,958 MY2025 Tiguans whose Body Control Module mishandles ECC errors, resetting mid-drive and disabling ignition, exterior lights, airbags and rearview camera. Dealers will reflash to BCM version 0326; owner letters follow on 6 November 2026.
items.so_what: Named account faces a software-defect recall touching airbags and drivetrain, remediated only in-workshop.

items.headline: Kigen automotive eSIM is first certified to GSMA SGP.32 v1.3
items.summary: Arm's Kigen unit achieved GSMA eUICC Security Assurance certification for an automotive eSIM on Infineon's TEGRION SLI22, the first to SGP.32 v1.3 with emergency-profile and post-quantum mitigations. OEM sampling in MFF2 and GSMA interoperability testing both begin October 2026.
items.so_what: Sets the reference security bar competitors must match to sell SGP.32 automotive eSIMs to long-life fleets.

deal.what: SGP.32 v1.3 automotive eSIM certified by GSMA

items.headline: Volkswagen and Elli set Q4 2026 launch of integrated V2G package in Germany
items.summary: Volkswagen and energy subsidiary Elli confirmed a Q4 2026 German launch of a bundled V2G offer combining an EV, bidirectional charger, smart meter, app and tariff, letting customers export stored power for revenue. Pre-registration opened June 2026.
items.so_what: First major OEM to sell V2G as a single retail bundle rather than a pilot, standardising the customer journey.

deal.what: Integrated V2G retail bundle for Germany

items.headline: Iridium, Deutsche Telekom IoT and Toyota send first NB-IoT satellite voice message
items.summary: On 10 September 2026, Iridium and Deutsche Telekom IoT demonstrated a standards-based NB-IoT voice message from a Toyota vehicle via Iridium LEO satellites, completing a global roaming agreement. Commercial availability for automotive and logistics customers is planned for Q4 2026.
items.so_what: Named-account OEM validates a live NB-IoT NTN path for connected-vehicle services beyond cellular coverage.

deal.what: Global NB-IoT NTN roaming agreement with Toyota demo

items.headline: NHTSA grants Zoox first commercial exemption for a purpose-built robotaxi
items.summary: NHTSA granted Zoox a temporary exemption allowing up to 2,500 purpose-built robotaxis annually for two years, the first for a driverless vehicle without conventional controls. The agency also signalled FMVSS updates and is developing National Competency Standards for ADS-equipped vehicles.
items.so_what: Creates a US legal route to scale non-conventional robotaxis before FMVSS is rewritten.

sources.outlet: Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety citing NHTSA

items.headline: FCC adds foreign humanoid and quadruped robots to Covered List
items.summary: FCC Public Notice DA 26-786 added foreign-produced networked robots over 4.4 lb to the Covered List on 28 July 2026, citing remote-takeover and supply-chain risks. New foreign models require conditional approval; previously authorised units are grandfathered through 2029.
items.so_what: Ties robotics market access in the US to cybersecurity and origin, reshaping OEM sourcing decisions.

items.headline: Rivian recalls 100,700 vehicles over prompt obscuring rearview camera
items.summary: Rivian filed a recall on 23 September 2026 covering 2022–2026 R1T, 2022–2027 R1S and 2027 R2 vehicles because a stability-control prompt can obscure the rearview image in reverse, breaching FMVSS 111. Over 95% of affected vehicles already carried the OTA fix.
items.so_what: Illustrates recalls becoming administrative closure of already-deployed OTA remedies, not workshop events.

items.headline: GM launches OnStar Fleet Intelligence platform
items.summary: On 30 September 2026 GM unveiled OnStar Fleet Intelligence, a centralised service integrating factory-embedded vehicle data with connected services to optimise asset utilisation, risk and operating cost for fleet managers. The launch extends OnStar's B2B position against aftermarket TSPs.
items.so_what: Named-account OEM pushes deeper into fleet telematics using its own embedded data as the baseline product.

items.headline: Thales and four APAC operators deploy multi-network IoT eSIM using SGP.32
items.summary: Thales, Singtel, Optus, AIS and Globe Telecom launched a multi-operator IoT eSIM network based on GSMA SGP.32, letting connected vehicles and fleet devices switch between participating networks across borders without SIM replacement. The rollout targets the automotive and commercial-fleet segment.
items.so_what: First live cross-border SGP.32 deployment in Asia-Pacific for vehicle and fleet devices.

deal.what: Multi-operator SGP.32 IoT eSIM network for vehicles

items.headline: Komatsu and EARTHBRAIN partner with AIM Intelligent Machines on autonomous dozers and excavators
items.summary: Komatsu and subsidiary EARTHBRAIN announced a partnership with AIM Intelligent Machines to deliver autonomous bulldozers and excavators in the US and Japan, integrating AIM's physical-AI stack with Komatsu's Smart Construction platform. US deployment is underway; Japan follows in 2027.
items.so_what: Named agri/industrial account commits to a physical-AI autonomy stack across two flagship machine categories.

deal.what: Autonomy partnership for dozers and excavators in US and Japan

items.headline: IEA publishes first standalone V2G report finding 75% cut in transformer overloads
items.summary: The IEA released its first dedicated V2G report on 25 September 2026, concluding bidirectional charging could prevent three-quarters of distribution-transformer overloads by 2050 versus uncontrolled charging, based on San Francisco modelling. Inconsistent standards are the main commercial barrier.
items.so_what: Puts V2G on the agenda of grid regulators worldwide with a concrete infrastructure-avoidance number.

items.headline: Toyota recalls 8,521 2026 C-HR EVs for BEV ECU software allowing battery overcharge
items.summary: NHTSA recall 26V570000 covers 8,521 MY2026 Toyota C-HR EVs built February–July 2026 after a Denso ECU software flaw can allow regenerative braking to overcharge the traction battery and trigger a full drive shutdown. Dealers apply a software update; owner letters began mid-October 2026.
items.so_what: Named-account EV recall centres on battery-management software, a growing category of electric-drive defects.

items.headline: China's CSRC applies three-criteria guidance to cool humanoid-robot IPO pipeline
items.summary: China's securities regulator informally told humanoid-robot IPO applicants they must demonstrate sustainable revenue, a three-year loss-narrowing forecast and ownership of core technology. The guidance followed Unitree's Shanghai debut, which surged nearly 500% before retreating sharply.
items.so_what: Raises the listing bar for at least two dozen embodied-AI companies filed in Hong Kong and Shanghai.

items.headline: NHTSA calls 'Recalls Next' meeting on OTA updates and technological innovation
items.summary: NHTSA published a Federal Register notice in late September 2026 announcing a public meeting on how connected-vehicle technologies, OTA updates and mobile repair are reshaping recall remediation, framing OTA as a tool to reduce recall time and burden.
items.so_what: Signals US regulator moving to codify OTA's role in recall procedure, affecting all connected-vehicle OEMs.

items.headline: Stellantis rebrands Mobilisights as Mobilisights Connect and expands B2B fleet offer
items.summary: Stellantis rebranded its connected-vehicle data division as Mobilisights Connect and broadened its B2B software offer with APIs and tools tied to factory-embedded telematics for fleet managers. The move intensifies competition with aftermarket TSPs on remote diagnostics and usage analytics.
items.so_what: OEM data business steps directly onto TSP turf, using embedded telematics as its default distribution.

items.headline: NMFTA reveals Bendix EC80 truck brake recall silently patched remote code execution flaws
items.summary: At Black Hat USA 2026, NMFTA researchers disclosed that a 2024 safety recall for Bendix's EC80 brake controller also fixed cyber vulnerabilities, including a wirelessly reachable remote code execution flaw and a hardcoded password able to disable traction control. Security fixes were not publicly disclosed.
items.so_what: Raises questions about transparency when safety recalls also carry undisclosed cybersecurity remediations.

items.headline: EU Data Act one year on: OEM APIs live, fleet data access nearing commodity
items.summary: A September 2026 Optivo analysis found all major automotive groups completed API infrastructure between October 2025 and March 2026 to expose telematics data to third parties under Regulation (EU) 2023/2854. Fleet managers can nominate telematics recipients without OEM contracts, though EU adoption remains uneven.
items.so_what: Confirms the EU has moved from mandate to live infrastructure, shifting negotiating power to fleet operators.

items.headline: Waymo recalls 3,791 robotaxis after ADS failed to stop on flooded road
items.summary: NHTSA reported that Waymo recalled 3,791 vehicles with 5th- and 6th-generation ADS after a driverless vehicle failed to stop on a flooded high-speed road, with a 100% assumed defect rate. All affected units received an OTA fix by 20 April 2026.
items.so_what: Established robotaxi operator uses OTA to close a safety recall covering its entire ADS fleet.

items.headline: CSA Group reissues intent to publish EV charger cybersecurity standard
items.summary: CSA Group reissued a public notice of intent for a Canadian cybersecurity standard covering all EV charging equipment, from residential Level 1/2 to DC fast chargers and V2G units, across design, procurement, operation and decommissioning. A second comment period ran through 30 June 2026.
items.so_what: Signals a formal North American cyber baseline for charger OEMs and CPOs is close to publication.
